The post says the first Android Clipper was found outside Google Play by Dr. Web in August 2018 and inside Google Play by ESET in February 2019.

67cf09802cdaf5f19447d7f8ddfac52ce688cd30.summary: Check Point Research's DFIR case study of The Gentlemen ransomware-as-a-service (RaaS). An affiliate tried to deploy SystemBC proxy malware during an incident response case, and the report counts over 1,570 SystemBC victims, mostly in the United States. The intrusion used Domain Admin access, Cobalt Strike, PsExec, Group Policy deployment, Defender tampering, AnyDesk and RDP. It ended with Windows, Linux and ESXi lockers that encrypt data and claim exfiltration.

hedges: The precise initial access vector could not be conclusively determined.
Whether SystemBC is directly integrated into The Gentlemen ecosystem or is simply a tool used by one affiliate remains unclear.
Check Point Research has no evidence to determine the exact nature of the SystemBC relationship.
It is likely that most SystemBC victims are companies and organizations, since SystemBC is typically used in human-operated intrusions.
The group appears to maintain an X account; the report says its posts likely aim to increase pressure on victims to pay.
The Gentlemen ransomware appears to be under active development.
Detection results for the ESXi variant may be affected by the password requirement, though this does not appear to affect Windows samples.
Several ATT&CK mappings are marked as inferred, implied or partly inferred in the report.
